q: Britain’s Slavery Abolition Act ends slavery in most of the British Empire.
The Sword Edict strips the samurai class of its blades.
The United States purchases Alaska from Russia.
The bloodiest day of the war ends Lee s first invasion at Antietam.
A pandemic sweeps the Roman legions home from the Euphrates.
The Moon landing is broadcast live to six hundred million viewers.
Apollo 11 lands on the Moon.
An oxygen tank ruptures and Apollo 13 loops around the Moon instead of landing.
Apollo 8 becomes the first crewed craft to orbit the Moon.
Apple Computer is founded in a garage in Cupertino.
The First World War ends with the armistice.
ARPANET sends its first message between two computers.
A telegraph message crosses the Atlantic for the first time, from Queen Victoria to President Buchanan.
Napoleon s masterpiece breaks the Austrians and Russians at Austerlitz.
John Logie Baird demonstrates the first working television.
Germany invades the Soviet Union with the largest invasion force ever assembled.
Henry V’s outnumbered army wins the battle of Agincourt.
Robert the Bruce defeats the English at Bannockburn.
William of Normandy defeats Harold Godwinson at Hastings and takes the English crown.
Nelson destroys the French fleet at anchor in Aboukir Bay.

n: The Fall of the Berlin Wall
q: The Berlin Wall falls.
The Black Death reaches Europe aboard Genoese merchant ships.
The bloodiest day of the Napoleonic wars is fought before Moscow.
The tea goes into the harbor as the town watches.
Richard III falls at Bosworth and the Tudor crown is won on the field.
Fidel Castro’s rebels enter Havana.
Parliament passes the Act that frees and rearrests the hunger strikers.
Charlemagne is crowned Emperor of the Romans in St. Peter’s, on Christmas Day.
The Chernobyl reactor explodes.
The children s crusade sets out for the Mediterranean and vanishes.
The last ship of Magellan’s fleet completes the first circumnavigation of the globe.
Columbus makes landfall in the Americas.
Japan makes schooling compulsory for every child.
The great powers convene at Vienna to redraw the map of Europe.
The delegates meet in Philadelphia to write a constitution.
The world waits out the thirteen days of the Cuban missile crisis.
The Curiosity rover lands on Mars.
D-Day: Allied forces land in Normandy.
Copernicus publishes De revolutionibus, placing the Sun at the center of the heavens.
The Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence.
Pierre and Marie Curie announce the discovery of radium.
The New York draft riots burn for four days.
The Eiffel Tower opens as the entrance arch to a world’s fair.
Lincoln s proclamation frees the enslaved in the rebellious states.
Charles I is executed after a public trial.
Ottoman forces under Mehmed II take Constantinople, ending the Roman Empire in the East.
Saigon falls and the Vietnam War ends.
The Alamo falls to Santa Anna’s army after a thirteen-day siege.
The last western Roman emperor is deposed, and the empire of the west ends.
Roosevelt takes the presidency to the family radio with his fireside chats.
The First Crusade captures Jerusalem.
Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reach the summit of Everest.
The first railway opens between Tokyo and Yokohama.
The first modern Olympic Games open in Athens.
Edward Jenner performs the first vaccination, inoculating a boy against smallpox with cowpox.
The First World War begins.
The American Civil War begins at Fort Sumter.
Roger Bannister runs the first four minute mile.
Parisians storm the Bastille.
The Norse invaders beat the northern earls outside York.
Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space, aboard Vostok 1.
Galileo observes the moons of Jupiter through his telescope.
The landings at Gallipoli are pinned on the beaches.
A hurricane drowns Galveston Island.
Mahatma Gandhi is assassinated in Delhi.

n: The Proclamation of the German Empire
q: The German Empire is proclaimed at Versailles, with Prussia’s king as emperor.
The three days at Gettysburg break the Confederate charge and the invasion.
The White Hurricane buries the northeast for days.
Three days of fire burn down Chicago.
The Great Exhibition opens in Joseph Paxton’s Crystal Palace in Hyde Park.
The Great Famine begins as potato blight destroys the crop.
The Great Fire of London destroys most of the old city in four days.
The Viking Great Heathen Army lands in East Anglia.
The Great Kanto earthquake levels Tokyo and Yokohama.
The Gunpowder Plot is foiled and Guy Fawkes is captured.
Gutenberg prints his 42-line Bible, the first major book made with movable type.
Gutenberg is first recorded with his movable-type press at Mainz.
The Haitian Revolution begins with an uprising of the enslaved.
William s army burns Yorkshire from the Humber to the Tees.
The Hindenburg burns at Lakehurst, New Jersey.

n: The Launch of the Hubble Telescope
q: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched.
Napoleon returns from Elba for the Hundred Days.
Hurricane Katrina breaches the levees of New Orleans.
The IBM Personal Computer goes on sale.
Ibn Battuta leaves Tangier on the first leg of a journey that will out-travel Marco Polo.
Napoleon invades Russia with the Grande Armée.
The Mongol fleets are scattered by the divine winds off Kyushu.
The iPhone goes on sale.
Jamestown, the first permanent English settlement in North America, is founded.
Napoleon shatters the Prussian army in a single day at Jena.

n: The Assassination of John F. Kennedy
q: President John F. Kennedy is assassinated in Dallas.
The July ultimatums turn a Balkan murder into a general war.
The largest armored battle of the war grinds the German army at Kursk.
The Mongol columns defeat the Polish knights at Legnica.
A Holy League fleet defeats the Ottoman navy at Lepanto.
The first shots of the Revolution are fired on the road to Concord.
The Civil War ends and Abraham Lincoln is assassinated.
Lindbergh flies solo from New York to Paris.
An earthquake and tsunami level Lisbon on All Saints Day.
The United States concludes the Louisiana Purchase.
The Louvre opens to the public as the republic’s national museum.
The Soviet Luna 2 probe becomes the first craft to reach the Moon.
Magellan’s expedition sets out to circle the globe.
King John seals the Magna Carta at Runnymede.
Nelson Mandela is elected President of South Africa.
The Athenian phalanx turns back the Persian landing at Marathon.
Sherman s columns cut a path from Atlanta to the sea.
The airborne attempt to bridge the Rhine falls short at Arnhem.
The Mayflower lands the Pilgrims at Plymouth.
The Meiji constitution creates Japan s first modern parliament.
Handel’s Messiah premieres in Dublin.
American carriers sink four Japanese carriers and turn the Pacific war.
Einstein publishes his miracle year papers, including special relativity.
Ford introduces the Model T.
Leonardo da Vinci begins painting the Mona Lisa.
The 19th Amendment is ratified, giving American women the vote.
Martin Luther posts his Ninety-five Theses.
Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species.
The Peasants’ Revolt reaches London and burns the Savoy Palace.
Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin.
The first recorded bubonic pandemic strikes Constantinople.

n: The Battle of the Plains of Abraham
q: Wolfe defeats Montcalm on the Plains of Abraham, and Britain takes Quebec.
Clive s victory at Plassey hands Bengal to the East India Company.
The Prague Spring ends under the tanks of the Warsaw Pact.
Newton publishes the Principia Mathematica.
The federal reconstruction of the South begins.
Revolutions sweep Europe from Paris to Vienna in the Year of Spring.
Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat, and the Montgomery boycott begins.
French soldiers digging a fort near Rosetta unearth a stone carved three ways.
The Roswell incident makes UFOs a household word.
The king speaks to the empire on the first royal Christmas broadcast.
Japan sinks the Russian fleet and joins the great powers.
The Mongols take Baghdad and end the Abbasid caliphate.
The Fourth Crusade, diverted from Jerusalem, storms and sacks Constantinople.
The Greek triremes trap the Persian fleet in the strait of Salamis.
Earthquake and fire destroy San Francisco.
A shot in Sarajevo kills the archduke and his wife.
Saigo s last stand at Shiroyama ends the samurai era.
The Second World War begins with the invasion of Poland.
The Seneca Falls convention declares the rights of women.
The September 11 attacks
William Shakespeare is born in Stratford-upon-Avon.
Shays indebted farmers close the courts of Massachusetts.
Japan s victory over China redraws the map of East Asia.
Europe’s leading physicists gather in Brussels for the first Solvay Conference.
The first day of the Somme costs the British army fifty-seven thousand casualties.
The Spanish Armada is defeated in the Channel and wrecked by storms on the way home.
The influenza pandemic circles the world at the end of the First World War.
The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite.

q: The first battle of the Wars of the Roses opens at St Albans.
Peter the Great founds St. Petersburg.
The German army at Stalingrad surrenders after the winter in the ruins.
Harold destroys the Norwegian invasion before marching south.
The Stockton & Darlington opens as the first public steam railway.
The Suez Canal opens to shipping.
The Summer of Love draws the young to the Haight.
Alexander Graham Bell is granted the telephone patent.
The Tet offensive sweeps into the cities of the south.
The Greek rearguard holds the pass until the last morning.
The kings of England, France and Sicily take the cross for Jerusalem.

Howard Carter opens Tutankhamun’s tomb.
The Continental Army winters starving at Valley Forge.

The fortress of Vicksburg surrenders on the Fourth of July and the river is Union.

n: The War of the Worlds Broadcast
q: The Mercury Theater s Martians panic the Halloween radio audience.
Napoleon is defeated at Waterloo.
The suffrage procession fills Pennsylvania Avenue the day before the inauguration.
The Woodstock festival gathers half a million on Max Yasgur s farm.
The Wright brothers make the first powered airplane flight.
